statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-70161 is a .NET SDK elevation of privilege issue in workload installation and advertising manifests: an attacker-controlled workload manifest ID can traverse paths under %ProgramData%\dotnet and import attacker-controlled MSBuild targets during elevated workload operations. Microsoft lists Windows as the only affected platform, and its list of affected SDKs names only .NET 10 and .NET 11 SDK feature bands; the .NET 9.0.21 release notes also list the CVE (https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/453, https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/56610, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.21/9.0.21.md). The elevated workload operations are those of the MSI-based workload installer: the SDK selects it only for MSI installs and throws an error instead when the operating system is not Windows (https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/v9.0.122/src/Cli/dotnet/commands/dotnet-workload/install/WorkloadInstallerFactory.cs). DHI dotnet9-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 9 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 242 packages of the eleven published builds (9.0.12-r0, 9.0.13-r0, 9.0.14-r0, 9.0.15-r0, 9.0.16-r0, 9.0.17-r0, 9.0.18-r0, 9.0.20-r0, 9.0.21-r0, 9.0.22-r0 and 9.0.23-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold: every build is a Linux SDK and runtime for x86_64 and aarch64, so dotnet workload commands use the file-based installer and the elevated Windows installer path is never reached in any published build.
